notes:
{栄枯|えいこ} is a literary word describing the cycle of prosperity and decline. It is composed of {栄|えい} (flourishing) + {枯|こ} (withering) — a metaphor from the natural life cycle of plants.

KEY EXPRESSION:
⟦{栄枯盛衰|えいこせいすい}→栄枯盛衰：07122_eikoseisui⟧ (rise and fall, vicissitudes of fortune) is a well-known four-character compound (⟦{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}→四字熟語：15663_yojijukugo⟧). The phrase ⟦{栄枯盛衰|えいこせいすい}→栄枯盛衰：07122_eikoseisui⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{世|よ}→世：00424_yo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{常|つね}→常：28958_tsune⟧ ("rise and fall is the way of the world") is a classic saying.

USAGE:
{栄枯|えいこ} is formal and literary. It appears in writing about history, empires, families, or businesses rather than in everyday conversation.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{盛衰|せいすい}→盛衰：05569_seisui⟧: rise and fall (similar meaning, slightly more common)
- ⟦{浮沈|ふちん}→浮沈：08128_fuchin⟧: ups and downs (more modern, used for careers, companies)
- ⟦{興亡|こうぼう}→興亡：05568_koubou⟧: rise and fall (of nations or empires)
